newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian regulator warns bank of maturity mismatch.
newsitem.headline: Belgian regulator warns bank of maturity mismatch.

text.p: Belgium's regulatory Banking and Finance Commission (BFC) has warned a Belgian bank, which it declined to name, of a maturity mismatch in its balance sheet and asked it to adjust the short term/long term ratio.

"One credit institution, which had built up an exceptionally high rate-risk compared to its financial reserves, has been ordered by the commission to reduce that risk within a certain period," the BFC said in its annual report.
"The fact that the maturity of liabilities is shorter than that of assets allows banks to make profits, but the risk involved must remain acceptable," BFC director Marcel Maes said.
Maes was speaking at the presentation of the BFC's annual report.
Banks typically gather short-term deposits which they convert in longer-term loans or bonds.

The current steepness of the Belgian yield curve -- three-month yields are just above three percent, while 10-year bond yields are at 5.91 percent -- allows banks to make an easy profit on the conversion.
But the bigger the maturity mismatch, the more banks are exposed to a sudden rise of short-term yields.

Banks can adjust the short/long ratio of the balance sheets by lengthening the liability side, shortening the asset side or by buying derivatives which limit their exposure to a rise in short-term rates.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
